entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (STXBP1, mouse neurons, lentiviral cDNA). Four of five missense variants leave total protein below 10 percent of wild type in direct-to-Laemmli lysates, while the mRNA of the transgene is unchanged (Supplementary Fig. 4a-c): a 'normal transcript, little protein' pattern for missense variants.
entries.snippet: Compared to WT Munc18-1, all mutants exhibited a significant reduction in protein levels, with four out of the five mutants resulting in protein levels below 10% of WT levels (Fig. 3a). This change was not due to changes in mRNA levels (Supplementary Fig. 4a–c).
entries.anchor: Results, Mutants of Munc18-1 are metabolically unstable, paragraph 1

entries.proposition: The reduced level is turnover, measured by two translation-independent or translation-blocked read-outs (cycloheximide chase and Dendra2 photoconversion), not by a degradation-inhibitor rescue: the paper reports no proteasome or lysosome inhibitor arm (0 occurrences of MG132 or bafilomycin in the article XML; the single chloroquine is the transfection step).
entries.snippet: Overall, these data support a direct effect of mutations on the metabolic stability of Munc18-1, and suggest structural destabilization of Munc18-1 as an underlying cause of Munc18-1-linked encephalopathies.
entries.anchor: Results, Mutants of Munc18-1 are metabolically unstable, last paragraph

entries.proposition: The solubility assay is a mild-detergent split: 0.1 percent Triton X-100 in PBS, one hour at 4 C, a 10-minute 13,000 g spin, soluble supernatant and pellet adjusted to equal volume and both run; the pellet is therefore measured, not discarded, which is the S/P arrangement a fractionation design needs.
entries.snippet: Insoluble material was pelleted by centrifugation (10 min at 13,000gav and 4 °C), the Triton X-100 soluble supernatant was transferred to a fresh tube, and the pellet was adjusted to the same volume with PBS.

entries.proposition: Insoluble aggregates are not cleared at the rate of soluble mutant and are not toxic by MTT and nuclear counts, so insolubility here is a stable pool, not a death signal.
entries.snippet: Although these insoluble aggregates were not cleared at the same rate as soluble Munc18-1 mutants, as assessed by a cycloheximide chase experiments of Triton X-100 soluble and insoluble fractions in Neuro2a cells (Supplementary Figs. 7a and 7b), aggregates were not toxic, as determined by an MTT assay (Supplementary Figs. 7c and 7d) and counting of neuronal nuclei in primary neurons and in Neuro2a cells (Supplementary Fig. 7e).

entries.proposition: Wild-type Munc18-1 is co-reduced in solubility by about a quarter when a mutant is co-expressed: the mutant acts on the wild-type pool (a dominant-negative or co-aggregation reading), which is specific to a hetero-oligomeric client and not a property a recessive or homozygous missense lesion needs.
entries.snippet: Strikingly, presence of mutant Munc18-1 reduced the solubility of co-expressed WT Munc18-1 by ~25%, in both primary neurons and in Neuro2a cells (Fig. 5d and Supplementary Fig. 10a), suggesting co-aggregation of mutant and WT Munc18-1.
